title: Agent State Graph Orchestration & Checkpointing
content: State graphs represent agent execution as a directed cyclic graph (DCG). Nodes encapsulate LLM calls or deterministic functions, while edges define conditional routing. Checkpointing persists state snapshots at each superstep, enabling pause-and-resume, time-travel replay, and human-in-the-loop review.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Standard for Tool Integration
content: Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides universal client-server interoperability for AI agents to discover, authenticate with, and invoke external enterprise tools and databases over stdio or SSE transports.

title: PostgreSQL 16 pgvector HNSW Index Tuning
content: In PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector, HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) indexes provide 95%+ recall on dynamic updates without needing index rebuilds. Key configuration parameters include m=16, ef_construction=64, and runtime parameter SET hnsw.ef_search = 40 for tuning latency versus recall trade-offs.

title: Postgres Error Code ERR_PG_40012: Lock Timeout in High Concurrency
content: Error code ERR_PG_40012 indicates an exclusive lock acquisition timeout during high concurrency transactions on partitioned tables. Resolution requires tuning lock_timeout and using advisory locks for optimistic concurrency control.

title: 256-Route Application Security Audit & OWASP Top 10
content: The 256-route API security audit evaluated endpoints against OWASP API Top 10 vulnerabilities, specifically closing Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) and enforcing strict role-based access control (RBAC).

title: Indian DPDP Act 2023 & GDPR Compliance Framework
content: Compliance under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 and GDPR requires purpose limitation, explicit consent capture, verifiable right-to-erasure workflows, and masking of personally identifiable information (PII) before external model dispatch.

title: Financial Multi-Way Transaction Reconciliation & Intellimatch
content: High-throughput reconciliation architectures implemented for tier-1 banks (ABN AMRO, Royal Bank of Canada) handle 1:1, 1:N, and N:M settlements, isolating out-of-proof transactions and maintaining mathematical double-entry ledger invariants.
